ENGL0150/Unit 1 · Foundations of Professional Healthcare CommunicationTopic 21–2 sessions

Foundations: Clear and Professional Communication

Workplace product

Professional patient or staff communication

Course goals advanced

  • 1. Grammar and Sentence Competency
  • 2. Professional Workplace Writing
  • 3. Patient-Centered Communication
1

Essential Question

Why does clear writing matter in healthcare?

2

Teaching & Learning Concepts

The communication principles, workplace expectations, and healthcare context behind this topic.

  • Communication is a patient-safety issue, not only a matter of politeness
  • What makes healthcare writing effective
  • Clarity, correctness, and professionalism are three different things — a message can be correct and still unclear
  • Audience and purpose: who is reading this, and what do they need to do after reading it?
  • Introduction to the Communication Check, the five criteria you will use throughout the course
3

Grammar Focus

A small set of high-value grammar skills, tied directly to this topic's communication task.

Diagnostic focus — a non-graded baseline

  • Parts of speech and what each one does in a sentence
  • Subject and predicate
  • Complete sentences
  • Subject–verb agreement
  • Capitalization
  • Basic punctuation
  • Fragments
  • Run-ons
  • Pronoun clarity
4

Healthcare Vocabulary

This topic's spelling and usage words. Earlier lists spiral forward — turn them on to review.

Word Bank — List 2

5

Formative Practice

Guided activities and short exercises. None of this is graded — it is here so you can find out what you know before it counts.

Grammar diagnostic

A baseline, not a grade. Answer honestly — the point is to find out what to work on, and every option explains itself.

Practice only — nothing here is graded or recorded.

  • 1Choose the sentence with correct subject–verb agreement.
  • 2Which of these is a sentence fragment?
  • 3Which sentence is a run-on?
  • 4Which sentence has a pronoun that is unclear about who it refers to?
  • 5Which sentence is capitalized correctly?
  • 6A coworker needs the updated supply list. Which message is appropriate for the workplace?
  • 7Which version of this instruction is clearest for a patient?
  • 8What is the complete subject of this sentence? “The new front-desk assistant verified the patient's insurance before the appointment.”

Words to spell — List 2

Flip each card for the meaning and an example.

6

Cumulative Workplace Product

Combine this topic's grammar, vocabulary, and communication skills into something you would actually produce at work.

Professional patient or staff communication

Write a short professional communication from the scenario below. It must apply this topic's grammar and spelling, use a professional tone, stay clear, and keep to objective language. Aim for four to six sentences — brevity is part of the skill.

Scenario

A patient has called the office asking to move an appointment that is scheduled for Thursday. The next opening with her provider is the following Tuesday at 10:00 a.m. She also asked whether she still needs to fast beforehand; the answer is yes, for eight hours. Write the message she will receive.

Submit through Brightspace. This page is for drafting and self-checking.

7

Revision & Reflection

Review your work against the Communication Check, then name one thing to improve next time.

Communication Check

Check your own writing against all five. Not graded — saved in this browser only.

Communication Check — check each criterion your writing meets

Think about

  • Read your draft out loud. Where did you stumble? That is usually where the reader will too.
  • Did you tell the reader what to do next, or only give them information?
  • Could someone outside healthcare understand every word you used?

Before You Move On

  • ☐Completed the grammar diagnostic
  • ☐Reviewed Word Bank List 2, including the confusable pairs
  • ☐Drafted the patient or staff communication
  • ☐Checked your draft against all five Communication Check criteria
